full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This first appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27-3-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 217 of 1997 dismissing the suit. 

 4. At the hearing of the suit two witnesses were examined on behalf of the plaintiffs including plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1. The plaintiffs filed documents which were proved and marked as Exhibits 1-5. On behalf of the con-testing defendants defendant No. 2(Ka) was examined as DW 1. On conclusion of the hearing of the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 27-3-2000 dismissed the suit, hence the appeal. 

 5. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submitted that Mahmuda Khatun who entered in to an agreement with the plaintiffs to sell the suit property died before the filing of the suit leaving behind her brother and sisters as her legal heirs who did not deny the execution of the bainapatra by her and one the defendant being No. 2(ka) who disposed in Court on their behalf also categorically stated that they did not claim the suit property as they heard that the same was said to the plaintiffs by Mahmuda Khatun and that they had no objection if the plaintiffs got the kabala through Court, the Court below ought to have decreed the suit. Mr Bhuiyan further submitted that the Court below was also wrong in finding that there was no proof that Mahmuda Khatun took possession of the suit property and that the plaintiffs got possession from Mahmuda Khatun. He submitted that in the plaint it having been categorically stated that possession of the suit property was handed over to Mahmuda Khatun on 8-11-1993 by RAJUK and the said assertion having not been challenged by the defendants no document or paper was required to be filed to prove the fact of possession of Mahmuda Khatun. Mr. Bhuiyan by referring, to Annexures A and B to the application filed under Order LXI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) further submitted that the two documents clearly show that deceased Mahmuda Khatun authorised Md Nazrul Haque, the son of plaintiff No. 1 to take possession of the suit plot and in fact, possession was delivered to him on 8-11-1993, but "due to inadvertence" those documents could not be filed which may be accepted as additional evidence. Mr Bhuiyan further submitted that the reasons assigned by the Court below in disbelieving the plaintiffs Bainapatra as being not proper (সঠিক নয়) are against the evidence on record as well as term No. 19 of the letter of allotment, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside and the suit be decreed. 

 9. We have gone through the documents annexed to the application for adducing additional evidence which show that deceased Mahmuda Khatun by filing application to the RAJUK authorised Md Nazrul Haque by attesting his signature to take delivery of possession of the suit plot from RAJUK on her behalf and accordingly, possession was delivered to Md Nazrul Haque on 8-11-1993. But neither these facts were stated in the plaint nor the documents were filed at the time of hearing of the suit. From the impugned judgment and decree it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge found fault with the deed of agreement on the ground that the same was entered into in violation of clause 19 of the letter of allotment. We have considered the letter of allotment, we find no bar in entering into an agreement by the lessee to transfer her allotted plot, here the suit property, particularly when RAJUK already executed and registered the lease deed in her favour in the meantime. It is necessary to state that the plaintiffs filed all the original documents relating to the suit plot, such as letter of allotment, the receipts show payment of instalments and the original lease deed at the hearing of the suit which facts prima facie prove the genuineness of the Bainapatra executed by Mahmuda Khatun. It is also a fact that DW 1 categorically stated that they had no objection if the plaintiffs got the kabala through Court. 

 11. In the result, this appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree is set aside. The suit is sent back on remand to the trial Court for hearing afresh giving the plaintiffs chance to amend the plaint in the light of the discussions made hereinbefore and adduce evidence afresh. If the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property as claimed in the application filed under Order LXI, rule 27 of the Code their possession therein shall in no way be disturbed by RAJUK till disposal of the suit.
